title: LLM parser: fixture corpus and real-API evaluation
description:
Make parsing actually good. Build a corpus of realistic sample emails with expected results, an opt-in script that runs them through the real API, and tune the prompt until they pass.

- Fixtures in packages/worker/test/fixtures/emails/parse/: for each case an .eml and an expected.json. Write realistic synthetic emails (do not copy real personal data): multi-leg round-trip flight for two travellers; airline schedule-change notice for one of those legs; hotel booking with a PDF confirmation; hotel cancellation; restaurant reservation; train ticket with PDF; rental car; timed museum/tour ticket; a forwarded booking (Fwd: with quoted headers); a non-English booking; a marketing newsletter; a plain receipt.
- packages/worker/scripts/eval-llm.ts (`pnpm --filter @planfully/worker eval`): runs parseEmail on each fixture with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .dev.vars, compares with expected.json (event count, type, start/end local+tz, confirmation, participants, status; name and location compared loosely), prints a pass/fail table and token usage per email.
- Iterate on prompt.ts until every fixture passes on three consecutive runs.

Owns: test/fixtures/emails/parse/, scripts/eval-llm.ts; may edit src/llm/prompt.ts and parse.ts.
Needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in packages/worker/.dev.vars. If it is missing, stop and leave a note; do not fake results.
The eval script is opt-in and must not run as part of `pnpm test`.
Fixtures with PDFs: generate small real PDFs (e.g. with a script) rather than fake bytes.
If a fixture cannot be made to pass reliably with Haiku, say which and why in the closing note instead of weakening the expectation.
acceptance_criteria: The eval script passes every fixture on three consecutive runs against the real API; results table and approximate cost per email are pasted into the closing note; mocked unit tests still pass.
notes:
From PR #7 review: (a) confirm root-array eventsJsonSchema is accepted live (docs show a root array example); (b) one invalid array element currently fails the whole response -> consider per-element validation keeping valid events; (c) any non-empty text/plain wins over HTML, so 'view in browser' stub text parts yield zero events -> prefer HTML when text is a short stub; (d) max_tokens is retried with an identical request.
From PR #17: dedupe tags for transport use placeKey(location.name), which only trusts a parenthesised IATA code, a bare code, or one next to an airport/terminal marker. Have the prompt ask for flight location.name as 'City Airport Name (IATA)' and train stations by their official name, so tags match across booking and change emails. 'today' is the UTC day of the Date header.

title: Timeline scale and layout (pure functions)
description:
The geometry of the timeline as pure, unit-tested functions, with no React. The view (planfully-gy4.6), zoom, lanes and the weather strip all build on these.

- timeline/scale.ts: TimeScale, makeScale(originMs, pxPerHour), plus tick generation: ticks(scale, fromMs, toMs, tz) -> { ms, label, kind: 'hour'|'day'|'week' }[] choosing density from pxPerHour (hours when zoomed in, days, then weeks).
- timeline/layout.ts: layoutEvents(events, scale, lanes) -> { lanes, blocks, unscheduled } as in CONTRACTS.md section 7.
  - lanes mode 'none': one lane. 'type': one lane per EventType present. 'participant': one lane per roster member; an event appears in each participant's lane; participants [] appears in every lane.
  - within a lane, overlapping events are packed into side-by-side columns (interval-graph colouring); each block reports column and columns so the view can size it.
  - minimum block height (in px) so point events and short events stay tappable; this affects overlap detection.
  - multi-day events (lodging) are ordinary long blocks.
  - events without start go to `unscheduled`.
- helper initialScrollMs(events, nowMs): now if within [first start, last end], else first start.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md section 7 (Timeline), CONTRACTS.md sections 2, 7.

title: Ingest pipeline: parse, geocode, dedupe, seal, append
description:
The default email route (packages/worker/src/email/routes/default.ts): ParsedEmail in, sealed records out.

1. events = await parseEmail(email, { roster: trip.roster, today, apiKey }). If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset, or parseEmail throws, or it returns [], go to the fallback (step 5).
2. Seal and putBlob each email attachment that at least one event references (once per attachment, new UUID each) -> Attachment { kind: 'file' }.
3. For each ParsedEvent: geocode location and endLocation; build Event { id: new uuid, ...parsed, attachments: [its files..., email.sourceAttachment], source: 'email', createdAt: now }.
4. dedupe = event.confirmation ? await dedupeTag(trip.dedupeKey, event.type, event.confirmation + (leg discriminator)) : null. For multi-leg bookings one confirmation covers several events, so the tag input must also include something stable per leg: use `${confirmation}|${location.name ?? ''}|${endLocation.name ?? ''}` for transport types and the plain confirmation otherwise. sealJson({ kind: 'put', event }) and appendRecord with the tag.
5. Fallback: one Event { type: 'other', name: email.subject || '(no subject)', needsReview: true, attachments: [all email files sealed..., sourceAttachment], source: 'email' } appended with no dedupe tag.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md sections 4, 5; CONTRACTS.md sections 3, 4, 6.

Owns: packages/worker/src/email/routes/default.ts and its tests. Uses, without modifying: parseEmail, geocode, putBlob, appendRecord, shared crypto.
A schedule change keeps origin and destination, so the per-leg tag stays stable and the new times fold into the existing event; a cancellation notice folds in as status cancelled. If the leg discriminator proves unreliable in tests (e.g. airport naming differs between emails), prefer normalising to IATA codes found in location.name; record the final rule in CONTRACTS.md section 3.
Errors in one event must not stop the others; if everything fails, fall back.
Never log email or event content.
Tests in the Workers pool with parseEmail's client and fetch mocked; open the stored records with the test trip's private key and fold them.

title: LLM parser module: email -> ParsedEvent[]
description:
parseEmail() in packages/worker/src/llm/parse.ts: one call to Claude Haiku 5.5 (model id `claude-haiku-5-5`) that turns a ParsedEmail into ParsedEvent[] (CONTRACTS.md section 6). This bead builds the module with a mocked client; tuning against the real API is the next bead.

- Input to the model: subject, date, a cleaned text rendering of the body (prefer text/plain; otherwise strip HTML to text, keep table structure readable, drop scripts/styles/tracking), PDF and image attachments passed natively, the roster (id, name, aliases), and today's date.
- Output: structured output constrained to eventsJsonSchema from @planfully/shared; then validate with zod. On invalid output retry once, then throw ParseError.
- Prompt (src/llm/prompt.ts), rules to state:
  - one event per flight leg, per train/bus/ferry segment, per lodging stay, per reservation or ticket
  - times are local wall-clock times at the place, with the IANA zone of that place; never convert
  - flights and other transport: location = origin, endLocation = destination; include airport codes in location.name
  - participants: map each traveller name onto a roster id using names and aliases (airline format 'SURNAME/GIVEN MR'); if no named traveller, use []; never invent ids
  - confirmation: the booking reference/PNR, not ticket or loyalty numbers
  - status 'cancelled' for cancellation notices; changes are returned as the updated event with the same confirmation
  - attachmentIndexes: which of the email's attachments belong to this event
  - leave unknown fields out; never guess; return [] for marketing, newsletters or anything that is not a booking
- The roster and email content are data: instruct the model to ignore any instructions inside them.

title: Email handler: routing, allowlist, MIME parse, store raw
description:
The Worker's email() entry point up to, but not including, turning an email into events.

1. Recipient -> local part -> split at the first '+': address and suffix (lowercased). Look up the trip with getTripByAddress. Unknown address or wrong domain: message.setReject('unknown address').
2. Sender check: the From header address (lowercased) must be in trip.allowedSenders AND the message must pass SPF or DKIM for that domain. Otherwise drop silently (no reject, no writes, no LLM).
3. Read the raw message bytes once. Seal them with the trip public key and putBlob; build sourceAttachment { id, filename: '<subject>.eml', mime: 'message/rfc822', size, kind: 'source-email' }. This happens before parsing so a later failure never loses the email.
4. Parse MIME with postal-mime into ParsedEmail (CONTRACTS.md section 6).
5. Call routes[suffix] ?? routes[''] inside ctx.waitUntil, catching and logging errors without content.

Create routes/default.ts and routes/receipts.ts as stubs that do nothing; the pipeline and receipts beads fill them in.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md section 5, CONTRACTS.md sections 4, 6, 8.

Check current Cloudflare Email Workers docs for the message object (raw stream, headers, setReject) and for how SPF/DKIM results are exposed (Authentication-Results / ARC headers); do not guess. If authentication results cannot be read reliably, implement the allowlist check alone, record that in CONTRACTS.md and in the closing note, and file a follow-up bead.
Forwarded mail: the allowlisted sender is the person forwarding, which is what From shows; do not try to look inside the forwarded message.
CPU budget: read the stream into one Uint8Array, avoid extra copies and string conversions of attachments.
Never log subject, body, addresses or attachment names.
Tests: build a fake ForwardableEmailMessage from a fixture file.

- roster of 3 people; some events for one person, some for two, some for everyone ([])
- two flights crossing time zones (with endLocation), a train, a rental car
- two lodging stays spanning several nights, in two cities
- dining and activities, including two that overlap in time
- 4 unscheduled attractions with only a location
- one cancelled event
- one booking sent twice: two put records with the same dedupe tag, the second with a changed time (must fold to one event)
- one event followed by a patch record, one followed by a delete record
- 3 receipts with attachments; one PDF, one PNG and one source-email attachment overall (generate tiny valid files in the script)
- all located events have real lat/lng

Also export the sample data builder from packages/worker/scripts/sampleTrip.ts so tests elsewhere can reuse it.

RETURNING next_seq` then insert. seq strictly increases and is never reused, even after deletes.
- src/api/records.ts: GET ?since=N (default 0) -> { records, latestSeq } ascending; POST { ciphertext (base64), dedupe? } -> 201 { seq }; DELETE /:seq -> 204 (idempotent).

Web api.getRecords defaults since=0 and the contract returns seq > N, so seqs must start at 1.

title: shared: log folding and merge rules
description:
Implement fold() and planCompaction() in packages/shared/src/fold.ts exactly as CONTRACTS.md section 3. Pure functions over already-decrypted records; no crypto, no I/O.

The rules that matter and must each have a test:
- puts sharing a dedupe tag, or sharing an event id, are one event; id is the earliest put's id, others are aliases
- later put wins per field, attachments union by id
- fields set by a patch are pinned and are not overwritten by a later put with source 'email'
- cancelled sticks across later email puts
- delete is a pinned deleted flag; deleted events are omitted from output and stay deleted when a later email for the same booking arrives
- patch/delete with unknown target is ignored
- input order does not matter (sort by seq first)
- planCompaction output folds to the same events, also when old and new records coexist

title: Calendar (.ics) export of filtered events
description: Generate in the browser. One VEVENT per scheduled filtered event with correct zones (TZID or UTC), location, confirmation in description, cancelled status. Stable UIDs so re-import updates instead of duplicating.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md sections 2, 7.

Owns: packages/web/src/export/ics.ts (+ tests); adds a 'Calendar (.ics)' item to ExportMenu.tsx (created by the PDF bead).
Write the generator by hand (no dependency): buildIcs(events, tripName) -> string, pure.
Per scheduled event one VEVENT: UID `${event.id}@planfully`, DTSTAMP, DTSTART/DTEND as UTC instants (`...Z`) computed with toInstant (avoids shipping VTIMEZONE definitions), SUMMARY, LOCATION (name, address), GEO when coordinates exist, DESCRIPTION with confirmation, participants and notes, STATUS:CANCELLED when cancelled. title: Weather data: Open-Meteo client and location-per-hour
description: Pure resolver: for each hour in view pick the location of the event in progress, else the most recent located event (arrival point for transport). Group hours into (lat,lng rounded, date range) requests to Open-Meteo hourly forecast: temperature, wind speed, precipitation. Cache in memory by key. No data beyond the forecast horizon (~16 days) or in the past; return gaps explicitly. Units setting (C/F, km/h/mph).
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md section 7 (Timeline, weather), CONTRACTS.md section 7.

Owns: packages/web/src/weather/resolve.ts, openMeteo.ts (+ tests). No UI.
resolve.ts (pure): hourlyLocations(events, fromMs, toMs) -> segments { fromMs, toMs, lat, lng, label }[]. For each hour: the located event in progress wins (for transport in progress use the destination); otherwise the most recent located event that has ended (its endLocation if transport, else location); before any located event, the first upcoming one. Ignore cancelled and unscheduled events. Merge consecutive hours with the same place (round lat/lng to 2 decimals).
openMeteo.ts: fetchHourly(segment) -> { timeMs[], tempC[], windKph[], precipMm[] } from the Open-Meteo forecast API (hourly temperature_2m, wind_speed_10m, precipitation; timezone=UTC so times are instants). Clamp requests to the available window (past days and ~16 days ahead; check current docs for exact limits); outside it return an empty series, not an error. In-memory cache keyed by rounded lat/lng + date range, 30-minute lifetime.
useWeather(fromMs, toMs) hook returning { series by segment, status }.
Units helpers: C/F and km/h / mph, default from navigator.language.
Tests mock fetch; never call Open-Meteo in tests.
acceptance_criteria: resolve tests: stay in one city; travel day switches from origin city to destination at departure; gap before first event; cancelled ignored. Client tests: builds the expected URL, parses a recorded response, returns empty beyond the forecast window, second identical call uses the cache.
close_reason: PR #19 merged. weather/resolve.ts hourlyLocations, openMeteo.ts fetchHourly (shared in-flight w/o abort, 30min cache + 1min negative cache, 100-entry cap, coverage field for no-forecast bands), useWeather per-segment status, units.ts. Contract in CONTRACTS.md §7.

title: Geocoding: server module and /api/geocode proxy

Geocoding for parsed and manual events.

Calls Google Geocoding (or Places Text Search when only a venue name is known) with GOOGLE_MAPS_SERVER_KEY, fills lat, lng, placeId and a formatted address. Returns the input unchanged when: the key is unset, loc already has lat/lng, loc has neither name nor address, the API returns nothing, or the result is only an approximate/partial match for a vague query.
- src/api/geocode.ts: GET /api/trips/:id/geocode?q= -> { results: Location[] } (up to 5), behind the access-token middleware. Without a key: 200 with empty results.

Owns: packages/web/src/offline/db.ts (+ tests with fake-indexeddb); hooks into trip/store.ts and trip/attachments.ts; a recent-trips list on the landing page (/).
IndexedDB via `idb`, database 'planfully': stores trips { tripId, secret, meta, lastSeq, openedAt }, records { tripId+seq -> StoredRecord (still sealed) }, blobs { blobId -> sealed bytes }.
Store load order: read cached meta and records -> open, fold, render immediately -> then sync from the network (since = lastSeq) and write new records back. Offline: status 'ready' with an `offline` flag instead of an error.
Attachments: fetchAttachment checks the blob store first; after a network fetch, cache the sealed bytes. On first sync, prefetch attachments under 5 MB in the background; larger ones are cached when first opened. Show a small 'available offline' mark per attachment in the event sheet.
Landing page: list cached trips (name, last opened) linking to /t/<id>#<secret>; this is how an installed app gets back into a trip. 'Forget on this device' removes a trip's secret, records and blobs.
The secret is stored on the device in plain form by design; state that next to the forget action.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with fake-indexeddb: cache round-trip, load-from-cache-then-sync ordering, forget removes everything for that trip only. Manually on a production build: open the seeded trip online, go offline, reload: timeline renders and a cached attachment opens; the landing page lists the trip.
close_reason: PR #34 merged. offline/db.ts (idb 8.0.3, DB v1 with oldVersion-aware upgrade): trips{secret,meta,lastSeq,fullLoadAt,revokedAt}, records, blobs (tripId index). Store loads cache first then syncs; persists server-acked own writes and compaction puts; removeRecords mirrored; full resync after 7 days; 401/403/404 only sets revokedAt (landing shows 'Link no longer works'). fetchAttachment/uploadAttachment use the blob cache; <5MB prefetch. Landing RecentTrips with Forget. Raw secret kept in memory until first snapshot (CONTRACTS §7). Follow-ups: no blob cache cap/eviction; sequential prefetch; brief resync flicker for records settled mid-fetch. fh8.3 must add a v2 'queue' store and clear it in forgetTrip.

title: Offline edit queue
description: Write-path actions made offline are queued in IndexedDB (already sealed), shown as pending, and flushed in order on reconnect with retry.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then CONTRACTS.md sections 5, 7.

Owns: packages/web/src/offline/queue.ts (+ tests); wraps the sendRecord step in trip/actions.ts and blob uploads in trip/attachments.ts.
Queue store in IndexedDB: ordered items { id, tripId, kind: 'record' | 'blob', payload (already sealed), blobId?, createdAt }. Actions enqueue first, apply optimistically, then try to flush.
Flush: in order, one at a time; on network failure stop and retry on the `online` event, on window focus and with backoff; on 4xx drop the item and surface an error. A blob must be flushed before the record that references it (enqueue in that order).
On app start, pending queued records are opened and folded on top of the cached log so offline edits are still visible after a restart.
UI: a small 'N changes waiting to sync' indicator in the shell.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with fake-indexeddb and a mocked api: offline edit is visible immediately, survives a simulated restart, flushes in order when online, blob before record; a 4xx drops the item and reports it. Manually: edit offline, restart the app, go online, and the edit reaches the server (visible from another browser).
close_reason: PR #41 merged. offline/queue.ts: IndexedDB v2 'queue' store (sealed payloads), actions enqueue then flush FIFO under a per-trip Web Lock; network/5xx/408/429 stay queued, other 4xx drop + roll back + lastError (refused put drops its dependents; refused blob drops referencing records and names the file); 401/403/404 stall with 'Link no longer has access' + Discard. Queued records restored as temp records on start; pending counts queued so compaction waits. DB open has blocking/terminated handlers and a 3s timeout falling back to memory queue. 30s/120s send timeouts. TripShell shows a lastError banner. createTripActions(store, { queue? }). Known: duplicate after lost response can overwrite another device's edit; items for never-reopened trips never flush.

title: Log compaction
description: When the log for an event exceeds a threshold of records, write the merged record from the shared compaction plan, then delete the replaced seqs. Safe under concurrent clients: write first, delete after, folding tolerates both present.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md section 4, CONTRACTS.md section 3.

Owns: packages/web/src/trip/compact.ts (+ tests); a call from the store after a successful sync.
Use planCompaction(records) from @planfully/shared. For each plan item: sealJson(write.body) -> api.appendRecord({ ciphertext, dedupe: write.dedupe }) -> only after success, api.deleteRecord for each seq in deleteSeqs -> update the store's records.
Run at most once per session per trip, only when online and no writes are pending, and only for groups with 4+ records.
Safe if interrupted or if two clients compact at once: the write happens first and folding gives the same result with old and new records both present.
acceptance_criteria: Test with a mocked api: a group of 5 records becomes 1, deletes happen only after the append succeeds, a failed append deletes nothing, and fold output is identical before and after. Manually: seeded trip record count drops and nothing changes on screen.
close_reason: PR #24 merged. trip/compact.ts compactTrip: append compacted record first, delete originals after (404 ok), once per session; skipped when offline, pending>0 (rechecked before each append/delete) or skipped>0. Temp seqs in trip/tempSeq.ts. store.removeRecords(seqs). CONTRACTS §7 notes version-skew risk and that persisted caches (fh8.2/fh8.3) must apply removeRecords.

title: Current-location dot
description: Button that asks for geolocation permission and shows the user's position on the map, with re-centre. Handles denial gracefully.
design:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (Working a bead), then SPEC.md section 7 (Map).

Owns: a small control inside packages/web/src/map/.
navigator.geolocation.watchPosition while the control is on; dot plus accuracy circle; 're-centre' button; stop watching when turned off or the view unmounts. Permission denied or unavailable -> short inline message, control returns to off.
Geolocation needs a secure context: works on localhost and on the deployed HTTPS site.
acceptance_criteria: With permission granted the dot appears and re-centre works; with permission denied a message shows and nothing breaks; no geolocation request happens until the user turns the control on.

title: PDF export: Korean font and RTL (Arabic/Hebrew) text
description: From PR #40 (4yd): Korean, Arabic and Hebrew print '?' in the PDF. Korean needs a Noto Sans KR subset like JP/SC. Also: only one font per document, so mixed-script itineraries lose characters.

title: Time zone abbreviations: consistent source
